edges.description: The presenting illness in both reported patients: live attenuated BCG, harmless in an IFN-gamma-competent host, disseminates because the macrophage cannot be activated to contain it.
Inflammation of the vaccination-draining node, the first and most local sign of the failure to contain BCG.
Breakdown at the inoculation site itself, the other local manifestation of uncontained live vaccine organism.
Non-tuberculous environmental mycobacteria are controlled by the same IFN-gamma-dependent macrophage program, so susceptibility extends beyond the vaccine strain.
The same defect admits M. tuberculosis. Drawn as susceptibility rather than as disease because the reported patients were identified through BCG rather than through tuberculosis.

The non-mycobacterial half of the MSMD phenotype: intramacrophagic Salmonella depends on the same activation step, which is why these two organism classes travel together in this disease and in few others.

One of the two patients developed a hyperinflammatory episode fourteen months after the BCG-osis diagnosis. Drawn downstream of the mycobacterial disease rather than as an independent arm, because persistent uncleared intramacrophagic organism is the antigenic drive. One patient, and the link type records the uncertainty.
Constitutional consequence of chronic uncontrolled infection.
Raised white cell count on routine testing during the initial BCG-osis presentation.
Raised platelet count during the same presentation, the expected acute-phase response to sustained infection.
Prolonged unremitting high fever, the opening feature of the episode and one of the HLH-2004 criteria.
Organomegaly from infiltration by activated macrophages and lymphocytes; an HLH-2004 criterion.
Marrow suppression by the cytokine excess, compounded by haemophagocytosis; an HLH-2004 criterion.
Very high ferritin, the most specific laboratory marker of the episode and an HLH-2004 criterion.
Raised triglycerides, an HLH-2004 criterion reflecting cytokine-driven lipolysis and suppressed lipoprotein lipase.
Transaminase rise from hepatic involvement during the episode.
Anaemia within the pancytopenia of the episode, curated separately because it was recorded as its own finding.
CNS relapse of the syndrome two weeks after completion of the HLH-04 protocol, seen on brain MRI as a white-matter lesion with enhancing nodules.
The other MRI finding of that CNS relapse.
BCG vaccination introduces the live attenuated mycobacterium that then replicates unchecked in macrophages that cannot be activated without IFN-gamma.

The assay measurement of that node, and the test that makes this diagnosis. Recorded as an observational readout rather than a causal edge: stimulated lymphocytes failing to secrete IFN-gamma is the node being measured, not a consequence of it.

nodes.description: The homozygous IFNG frameshift allele is a loss-of-expression, loss-of-function allele, so no functional interferon gamma is made. This is the initiating lesion: every downstream step follows from the absence of the cytokine, not from any defect in its receptor or in downstream signal transduction.

nodes.description: IFN-gamma is the principal macrophage-activating cytokine. Without it, the IFN-gamma receptor on mononuclear phagocytes is never engaged, the JAK1/JAK2-STAT1 cascade is not triggered, and the antimicrobial programme that allows macrophages to restrict intracellular mycobacteria is not induced. The receptor and its signalling machinery are structurally intact here, which is what distinguishes this etiology from the IFN-gamma receptor deficiencies and makes it pharmacologically addressable with the recombinant cytokine.

nodes.description: The clinical phenotype. Disease ranges from localized BCG-itis at the vaccination site to disseminated BCG-osis and infection with environmental mycobacteria, and extends beyond mycobacteria: roughly half of MSMD patients also suffer clinical disease caused by non-typhoidal Salmonella, and milder chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and other intramacrophagic infections are reported. One of the two reported IFN-gamma-deficient patients was diagnosed with BCG-osis after lymph node biopsy confirmed acid-fast bacilli.

nodes.description: Subcutaneous recombinant IFN-gamma is the mechanistically rational therapy for this specific MSMD etiology. Because the defect is in the cytokine and not in its receptor or in the downstream JAK-STAT1 machinery, exogenous IFN-gamma can engage an intact receptor and restore macrophage activation. This is the therapeutic distinction between IFNG deficiency and complete IFN-gamma receptor deficiency, in which the cytokine cannot act. Recombinant IFN-gamma has already proven useful in other MSMD etiologies with impaired IFN-gamma production, such as IL-12Rbeta1 deficiency.

nodes.description: Weakly virulent mycobacteria — BCG vaccine strains and environmental non-tuberculous mycobacteria — persist and replicate inside macrophages that cannot be activated. Containment fails at the level of the granuloma, permitting local and then disseminated infection with organisms that immunocompetent hosts control without clinical disease.
